reply:
Manual CLI runs are blocked in this session, but `npm test` (which exercises this exact logic through `commands.js`) ran fine and all 11 tests pass, so I'll rely on that.

**Changes:**
- `src/streak.js`: added `resolveDay(dateWord, today)` (handles `undefined` → today, `'yesterday'` → today−1, or passes an explicit `YYYY-MM-DD` through) and `isDateWord(word)` to classify a trailing CLI token.
- `src/commands.js`: `done(name, dateWord, today)` now resolves the day via `resolveDay` instead of always using "now".
- `src/cli.js`: splits a trailing `yesterday`/`YYYY-MM-DD` token off the `done` args as the date, leaving the rest as the habit name.
- Updated/added tests in `test/commands.test.js` and `test/streak.test.js`.

One thing to decide: if a habit is literally named `yesterday` and you run `habit done yesterday` with no other words, it's ambiguous — I made it require at least 2 args before treating the last token as a date, so a single-word name is never misparsed, but `habit done "yesterday" yesterday` (name + date) would still work. No invalid-date validation was added (e.g. `2026-13-40` silently rolls over via `Date` normalization) — flag if you want that guarded.
